basis: Estadao (2021-06-02) on the $65M Series B: 'O aporte teve ainda participações de Tiger Global Managament, Softbank, Monashees e Lightspeed Venture Partners'; Portafolio calls Tiger a previous investor at that round, so the firm held the company through private rounds

note: B2B food supply marketplace for restaurants, founded in Bogotá (2018, Y Combinator 2019), later in Mexico and Brazil. Tiger took part in the $65M Series B of June 2021 as an existing investor (Estadao; Portafolio, Semana name Lightspeed as the new one); the round Tiger first entered, between the 2019 seed and the $25M Series A of April 2020 led by GGV and Monashees, is not on record, so the stage is undetermined. Frubana closed Brazil, its last market, in August 2025 (Portafolio, 2025-08-14): defunct (the Lightspeed row still reads private).

FTX Trading, the crypto exchange, Nassau. Tiger is named among the 69 investors of the $420.69M round of October 2021 at $25B (The Block), the first round tying the firm to FTX (not named in the July 2021 Series B release), and joined the January 2022 Series C at $32B: Growth. Chapter 11 from November 2022: defunct under the bankruptcy ruling, aligned with the IVP, Lightspeed, Ribbit and Sequoia rows.

Expense management software, Bengaluru. Tiger led the Series A of February-March 2019 ($4.2M; VCCircle, Mint), after a $1.1M seed in April 2018 without Tiger: the firm's entry. Steadview led a $4.5M round in October 2019.

basis: The recall headline (VCCircle, 2022-01-24) calls Classplus Tiger Global-backed and names Gaana only as its new finance executive's former employer; Gaana was funded by Times Internet and Tencent, and no record ties Tiger Global to a round of Gaana

note: Online skill gaming (RummyCircle, My11Circle), Mumbai. Tiger was the company's first institutional investor in 2011 (Wikipedia; VCCircle 2012 on the disclosed Tiger investment); no source names the round, so the stage is undetermined. Tiger joined the $75M round at $2.5B led by Malabar in March 2022 (Mint). Collapse evidence: India's August 2025 ban on real-money games ended its core business and layoffs followed (Moneycontrol, 2025-09-01); the stale 2022 mark no longer stands, so below $1B with no figure (agent reading, listed for review).

Ganji.com, online classifieds, Beijing. Tiger Global Mauritius Fund and Internet Fund II sign the registration rights agreement as selling Ganji holders when 58.com bought into Ganji in April 2015 for cash and 58.com shares (58.com's 20-F exhibit; Reuters, 2015-04-17); the two were combined under 58.com, so acquired. The round in which Tiger entered is not on record, so the stage is undetermined.

basis: Evan Feinberg on these Form Ds (2020-2023, Burlingame) is Genesis Therapeutics' founder and chief executive, listed as executive officer: a homonym of Tiger's Evan Feinberg (D7); no Tiger record names the company

note: B2B fashion and lifestyle sourcing platform, Gurugram. Tiger led the $28M Series B of April 2022 at over $160M (Business Line; Entrackr), its first round in the company: Growth. Multiples led a Series C of over $50M in February 2025.

Rapid grocery and food delivery, Istanbul. Tiger backed the $128M round of January 2021 (Business Insider headline) and the $300M round at $2.6B of March 2021 (Business Insider), the company's third and fourth rounds: Growth. Peak mark $11.8B (March 2022). After a 2024 restructuring under Mubadala's control, Uber agreed in February 2026 to buy Getir's delivery business in Turkey for about $335M, cleared by the Turkish Competition Board in June 2026: the core business was sold, so acquired (the Sequoia row still reads private, below $1B).

Independent mobile app store and ad network, founded in Lithuania in 2004 and based in San Mateo (WSJ, 2014), so US, not the pre-filled LT. Tiger's $25M Series C of February 2011 (the company's release) was its entry: Growth. Sungy Mobile bought GetJar in February 2014 for $5.3M in cash plus an earn-out (WSJ; VentureBeat): acquired.

basis: Evan Feinberg, a Tiger partner in tenure, is director on the June 2015 Form D ($8M) of GetNinjas Holdings Ltd., the Cayman parent of the Brazilian services marketplace, and GetNinjas reported in May 2021 that Tiger Global sold 3,008,034 shares in its IPO offering, cutting its stake to 13.4% (ADVFN): a pre-IPO position taken in a private round

note: GetNinjas, online marketplace for local service professionals, São Paulo; listed on B3 (NINJ3) in 2021. The Form D of June 2015 records an $8M sale with Tiger's Evan Feinberg as director, but no source names that round or says whether Tiger entered earlier, so the stage is undetermined. REAG Investimentos took control through a 2024 tender offer and used the listed company for its reverse IPO (Exame, 2025-01-28): acquired.

DevOps platform (Nasdaq: GTLB since October 2021), San Francisco address. Tiger Global Private Investment Partners XI and Tiger Global Investments sign the investors' rights agreement of 2019-09-10 that accompanies the Series E preferred (the IPO filing's exhibit), the $268M round led by Goldman Sachs and ICONIQ: Tiger's entry, Growth; no earlier Tiger round is on record. The agreement names a private-equity fund beside a public-desk fund, so the row stays on the home desk (X1 does not apply). Market cap replaces the SEC float: $7.81B (2026-09-25), as the Coatue row reads.

basis: Online Recruitment (2015-01-08): 'Glassdoor raises $70 million led by Google Capital and Tiger Global Management', a private round; Lee Fixel, in his Tiger tenure, is director on the company's 2015-2016 Form Ds

note: Jobs and company reviews site. Google Capital and Tiger led the $70M round of January 2015, Tiger's entry into a company founded in 2007 that had raised several rounds: Growth. The Form D band's Pre-Seed read a 2012 filing that predates Tiger. Recruit bought Glassdoor for $1.2B in 2018: acquired. City San Francisco as the Sutter Hill row reads (the Battery row reads Sausalito, the founding town).

Beauty brand, New York. Tiger joined the $100M Series D led by Sequoia (March 2019, Reuters via Yahoo), its first round in the company: Growth. The $1.8B mark of the 2021 Series E did not hold: the 2025 raise was sought at under $1B (Forbes, 2025-04-11, as the IVP, Sequoia, Spark and Thrive rows record), and the company raised again in 2026 after closing most stores; below $1B, aligned.

Aggregator of digital-first consumer brands, Bengaluru. Tiger Global and Flipkart Ventures led the company's $36M first round of July 2021 (This Week India), which Exchange4Media names its Series A: Tiger's entry. It raised $21M in 2024 and put its Pepe innerwear business up for sale in 2026.
